name: Qualitative or Quantitative Defects of Desmin

criteria.description: Presence of progressive skeletal muscle weakness predominantly affecting distal and proximal muscles
Muscle biopsy showing characteristic desmin-positive protein aggregates and myofibrillar disorganization
Identification of pathogenic variants in the DES gene
Evidence of cardiomyopathy or conduction defects on ECG or echocardiography
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive myopathy with muscle biopsy showing desmin aggregates and confirmation by genetic testing of DES mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by cardiac evaluation and family history but requires muscle pathology and genetic confirmation.

searchTerms: abnormal protein buildup in muscle fibers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive distal and proximal muscle weakness
searchTerms: gradual weakness in both distal and proximal muscles

common.symptomName: Muscle atrophy predominantly in distal limbs
searchTerms: muscle wasting in hands and feet
loss of muscle bulk in arms and legs

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to muscle weakness
searchTerms: fatigue during activity due to muscle weakness
poor exercise tolerance caused by muscle weakness
irregular heart rhythms including AV block

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion secondary to cardiac involvement

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to hypoventilation
searchTerms: weak breathing muscles causing low oxygen
hypoventilation due to respiratory muscle weakness
weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs
heart muscle disease leading to failure

rare.symptomName: Dysphagia due to involvement of oropharyngeal muscles
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to weak throat muscles

laboratory: Muscle biopsy showing desmin-positive protein aggregates
imaging: Echocardiography revealing cardiomyopathy or ventricular dysfunction
Chest X-ray or CT showing respiratory muscle weakness complications
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the DES gene identified by sequencing
other: Electrocardiogram showing conduction abnormalities such as AV block
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic mutations (e.g., in CRYAB, MYOT)
Variable muscle biopsy findings without desmin aggregates
Absence of desmin-positive aggregates on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Cardiac conduction abnormalities with syncope or palpitations
Family history of sudden cardiac death
references: Schröder R, Schoser B. Desmin-related myopathy. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:23.
Goldfarb LG, Dalakas MC. Tragedy in a heartbeat: malfunctioning desmin causes skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. J Clin Invest. 2009;119(7):1806-1813.
Orphanet: Qualitative or quantitative defects of desmin (ORPHA:209041)
